text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

An all-female panel is not evidence of anything on its own. Panel composition varies for mundane reasons, and in health care, laboratory and HR management are heavily female fields, so a four-woman panel is statistically unremarkable. Four people also form too small a sample to infer bias.

Your stronger point is substantive: the job description's weighting of leadership versus scientific depth, and whether it was applied consistently. "Broad leadership experience" may genuinely exceed heading one section — or may be thin. You can't tell yet.

The real issue is the unanswered request. Follow up in writing, cite any applicable transparency or equal-treatment rules, and set a deadline. Judge on the reasons given, not the panel's sex.
